rationale: In vivo genome-wide Brunello knockout screen in human SC-islets (from hESC) transplanted under the kidney capsule of NSG-MHC-null mice; half the mice received allogeneic human PBMCs (hPi grafts) and grafts were recovered 10 weeks later. One GEO sample (GSM6008413) holds a PoolQ count table with one column per mouse graft (sample_info: Ms #64/69/70/73/74/78 Ctrl = control grafts; Ms #65/67/68/72/76/79 = hPi grafts) plus pre-transplant, NTC and plasmid libraries, which are not used. Knockouts that let SC-islet cells escape allo-rejection are enriched in hPi grafts relative to control grafts. Ms #79 (hPi) is left out: it has 42,430 reads over 77,441 guides (78% zeros) and correlates at most 0.22 with any other library, a failed library. The paper modelled guide counts relative to non-targeting guides (KO x PBMC interaction against the NT guides), and immune rejection removes cells from hPi grafts, so totals are taken from the non-targeting controls ('totals': 'control'). Each mouse is its own library; mice are not paired across arms.
